Issued at 226 PM CDT Tue Sep 15 2026

Rest of Today - Thursday Night: Cooler Than Normal, Shower and Storm 
Chances Late Wednesday

Zonal to slight southwesterly upper-level flow with accompanying 
surface high pressure will dictate our weather conditions for the 
rest of today and throughout much of the daytime on Wednesday. 
Consequently, expecting fairly dry conditions for the rest of today 
and through the daytime hours on Wednesday with northwesterly flow 
today aiding in keeping temperatures cooler than normal with highs 
in the upper 60s to middle 70s. Cannot rule out some fog tonight, 
particularly north of I-94 where mid-level cloud cover manages to 
clear out, however confidence is low for areas south of I-94 to see 
much for fog at this point. Otherwise, continued dry conditions 
during the daytime hours on Wednesday will give way to some shower 
and storm chances Wednesday evening and into the overnight as some 
weak ripples in the 500mb flow push from west to east through the 
area. As a result, some of the CAMs generally indicate some shower 
and storm development where forcing may be marginally better. Given 
the fairly weak MUCAPE (only a couple of hundred J/kg) and 
precipitable waters of around 1.25-1.75" as this precipitation moves 
through, not expecting overly heavy rainfall producers with this 
particular round of rain. However, the grand ensemble 
(GEFS/EC/Canadian) has some modest probabilities (30-60%) for 
rainfall amounts over 0.25" so would not rule out some healthier 
rainfall amounts. 

Friday - Saturday: Widespread Rainfall Likely, Locally Heavy 
Rainfall Potential 

The most impactful period over the next 7 days appears to be Friday 
and into Saturday as a shortwave trough rolls off of the rockies and 
approaches the region. As this occurs, model guidance generally 
agrees on surface cyclogenesis taking place over the Great Plains 
with the resultant low pushing eastward into the Upper Midwest. With 
this low pushing towards the local area, a profound axis of 600-
800mb frontogenesis sets up over the region. While some uncertainty 
remains on where this axis sets up, however the heavy rain parameter 
space where this better forcing is present is quite substantial with 
NAM/GFS preciptable waters of around 1.5-2.0" and warm cloud 
depths in excess of 4km. Additionally, some weak MUCAPE present 
atop this frontogenetic layer would likely aid to enhance lift 
and precipitation production further. 

In response to this fairly robust forcing regime, the grand ensemble 
(GEFS/EC/Canadian ensemble) has fairly high probabilities 
(40-70%) already for rainfall amounts over 1" across the region,
mainly near and north of I-90. Additionally, the recent EC 
Extreme Forecast Index paints a shift of tails of 0 to 2 over 
the region, suggesting some members reaching the 99th percentile
of model climatology for rainfall. This is being driven 
primarily by the 95th percentile of the EC having members in the
3-5"+ ballpark within the heaviest axis of rainfall so cannot 
rule out these amounts in some locations. As a result, areas 
that receive any rainfall in this range will be susceptible to 
localized flooding and river rises. As far as severe potential 
is concerned, much of the warm sector with this system currently
is favored south of the local area and is displaced from the 
favorable shear with the surface cyclone. As a result, thinking 
that the severe potential at this point is fairly low for the 
local area which is generally reflected in the AI/ML guidance 
only having some 5% probabilities at the most across the local 
area. 

Overall, the main point of uncertainty with this setup is exactly 
where the heaviest rain will fall as there still remains some 
discrepancies between deterministic and ensemble models, including 
AI guidance, as to where the axis of heaviest rainfall will be. 
However, confidence is certainly increasing for fairly healthy 
rainfall amounts where this corridor of rain occurs. Consequently, 
areas that saw heavy rainfall in days prior may be susceptible to 
localized flooding concerns depending on where the heaviest rain 
falls. 

Early Next Week: Staying Cooler Than Normal, Additional Rain Chances

As the rainfall from Friday and Saturday departs the local area, 
northeasterly flow around the surface low will likely keep 
temperatures slightly below normal into Sunday with median high 
temperatures in the NBM hovering in the middle 60s to near 70. The
